title: Redwood discovery: model selection & deployment options - NexusMed Analytics
summary: Discovery call focused on open-model selection for clinical summarization and triage workflows. Customer has strict PHI/data residency requirements and is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for latency and compliance. Discussed context length needs (~32k), multilingual support, tool-calling for EMR connectors, and benchmarking next steps.
topics: Context length requirements (32k tokens, average 8k per doc)
Multilingual support (EN + ES + PT) and medical term fidelity
Tool-calling / function calling for EMR actions and retrieval
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Latency vs cost / batching and KV cache considerations
Security ask: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
next_steps: Maya to send Dedicated pricing + token estimator by 2026-10-07
Arjun to share benchmark plan and sample config for 32k context runs
Customer to provide redacted sample dataset and typical prompt set by 2026-10-09
Schedule a 60-min technical POC kickoff (SE-led) for week of 2026-10-12
action_items: Maya Chen - Send Dedicated + Hosted pricing breakdown and example cost model - 2026-10-07
Arjun Patel - Draft benchmark plan (32k context, multilingual, tool-calls) and required infra - 2026-10-08
Dr. Elena Ruiz - Share redacted sample EMR transcripts and prompt examples - 2026-10-09
Samir Gupta - Confirm security contacts for SOC2 and KMS questions - 2026-10-06
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-04 15:30 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Arjun Patel (Redwood) - Dr. Elena Ruiz, Samir Gupta, Liam O'Connor (NexusMed)
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Yup, loud and clear - thanks for doing this.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda: we want to cover your workload, model expectations (open models vs managed), deployment options - hosted/dedicated/private - and then next steps for a POC. Arjun is our SE and will jump into perf and model selection.
[00:28] Arjun Patel: Hey hi. So high level, why don't you kick off with your primary use-cases and constraints?
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Sure. We're building automated clinical summarization and triage, also routing to case managers. Data's PHI, we need EU+US residency for some cohorts, and we need a long context window, about 30k to 32k tokens, because notes are long.
[00:52] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Also multilingual - English, Spanish, and Portuguese - with accurate medical terminology. We saw hallucinations with some smaller models.
[01:05] Arjun Patel: Got it. So context length is a big driver. For open models there are variants that support 32k windows, but performance and cost vary a lot. We typically recommend evaluating both 32k-capable variants and a strategy of retrieval-augmented prompts + KV cache to reduce cost.
[01:25] Samir Gupta: Can you expand on KV cache? I've seen notes about KV 'cash' in some docs, apologies if I mis-read.
[01:33] Arjun Patel: No worries - KV cache, key-value cache, it's the attention cache for decoder models. We can persist prefixes for a patient so repeated calls are much cheaper and lower latency. In Redwood we surface caching and automatic prefix reuse; it helps a lot for repeated summaries.
[01:50] Maya Chen: One quick question on deployment: given PHI and residency, are you leaning toward Private or Dedicated?
[01:58] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Privacy first. Ideally Private in our VPC or even an on-prem option for the most sensitive cohorts. But cost and time-to-PoC matter.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: If Private is long lead, we might start on Dedicated reserved capacity in our region, then migrate.
[02:18] Arjun Patel: That's common. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and isolation, plus faster onboarding than full Private. We can design a migration path. For Private we support a private control plane and customer-managed networking, but it takes ~8-12 weeks depending on approvals.
[02:33] Dr. Elena Ruiz: What about hosted? Would hosted ever be acceptable for PHI?
[02:39] Maya Chen: Hosted can work if you have contractual commitments and data handling controls, but for PHI most customers go Dedicated or Private to keep everything in a VPC and control keys. Also customers ask for KMS integration and HSM support which is easier in Dedicated/Private.
[02:55] Samir Gupta: Ok noted. On models: we're interested in open models, not locked into any vendor. We tried a few - open weights - but we saw latency and cost spikes. Any recommendations?
[03:08] Arjun Patel: For clinical accuracy and 32k support, we usually evaluate variants of LlamaX-style models and Mistral/Redwood-verified variants that are quantized. Tradeoffs: full fp16 gives best quality but higher cost, 8-bit/4-bit quantization reduces cost but may impact rare medical terms. We'll run targeted evals.
[03:27] Dr. Elena Ruiz: How about tool-calling? We need the model to invoke EMR actions - like pull latest meds, write a draft note, or flag cases.
[03:36] Arjun Patel: We support structured function/tool calling. In the Hosted API it's streaming + function call safe. For Dedicated/Private, you also get the same API surface, we just ensure network policies. There's occasional terminology mismatch in transcriptions - the call might show 'function-calling' as 'function calling' or 'fanction call' - apologies - auto-transcript.
[03:54] Maya Chen: A quick dig into latency: what's realistic for a 32k summarization call?
[03:59] Arjun Patel: Depends on GPU and model variant. On our Dedicated A100-like pools you'll see 700ms to 2s per 1k tokens generation latency under steady load, but end-to-end for a 32k context with a 200-500 token summary might be 1.5-4s depending on batching and caching. If you need <1s SLAs we'd design for smaller context + retrieval or faster model family and pre-caching.
[04:23] Liam O'Connor: Cost ballpark? We need to justify cost per patient-summary at scale.
[04:28] Maya Chen: We'll share a cost model. Dedicated reduces per-token cost. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/caching and quantization profiles. I'll send an example.
[04:38] Dr. Elena Ruiz: On multilingual quality: we've seen Spanish degrade more than we'd like. Are there recommended models?
[04:45] Arjun Patel: Some open models are trained on multi-lingual corpora; others don't handle med terms. We'll evaluate using your Spanish/Portuguese prompts. We can also fine-tune or use instruction-tuning datasets for clinical language if needed. Fine-tuning on PHI requires Private/Dedicated modes for compliance.
[05:03] Samir Gupta: Security checklist: SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data residency. Can you confirm those?
[05:11] Maya Chen: Yes - SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC in Console, comprehensive audit logs, KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated, and region pinning for residency. We'll attach our security whitepaper.
[05:28] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Great. On integration, we want tool-calls to our EMR in a safe way (no write without approval). How do you handle confirmations?
[05:37] Arjun Patel: We recommend a pattern: model proposes action via function schema, we run the tool in a sandbox, and require a human-in-the-loop approval for write operations. You can enforce via route policies and role-based approvals in the Console.
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: Are there examples or reference architectures?
[05:55] Maya Chen: Yes - we'll share a reference doc and a small demo that shows function calling with a sandboxed EMR connector.
[06:03] Dr. Elena Ruiz: For the POC, can you support running benchmarks with our redacted records? We want comparisons vs OpenAI and Anthropic we already tried.
[06:12] Arjun Patel: Absolutely. We'll plan side-by-side comparisons: same prompts, same dataset, measure latency, token cost, hallucination rate on annotated set. We'll also include a Dedicated run and a Hosted run to compare.
[06:26] Samir Gupta: Will Redwood run the benchmarks in our VPC? For privacy.
[06:31] Arjun Patel: For the most sensitive data, we recommend either Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment. For initial benchmark you can provide redacted samples and we can run in Hosted with contractual protections, but if you prefer we can stand up a Dedicated benchmark cluster.
[06:46] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Timeline question - how quickly can we get a POC? We're aiming for pilot in Q4.
[06:52] Maya Chen: If you want Dedicated start, we can get a pilot in 2-3 weeks once contract and infra region are agreed. Private will take longer, roughly 6-12 weeks for full on-prem/VPC depending on approvals.
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: Good. On model telemetry: we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
[07:11] Maya Chen: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route/layer latency, tracing hooks, and error analytics. We'll show a dashboard during the POC.
[07:22] Dr. Elena Ruiz: About quantization - if we do 4-bit quant, do we risk missing rare medication names?
[07:29] Arjun Patel: There's risk; quantization can slightly degrade rare token fidelity. Our Optimize recommendations will run a small ablation: full precision vs 8-bit vs 4-bit on your terms. That helps choose acceptable tradeoffs.
[07:43] Samir Gupta: What about model rollouts and A/B testing? We want easy fallback to a safe model if we detect regressions.
[07:51] Maya Chen: We support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin production route to a stable variant and send a fraction of traffic to a new model. Automatic fallback can route to a smaller model on overload.
[08:05] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Are there limits on function-calling complexity? Like nested calls?
[08:11] Arjun Patel: The API supports structured nested calls but best practice is to keep schemas explicit. For complex workflows we orchestrate with a lightweight orchestrator outside the model and use the model for decision and content generation.
[08:25] Liam O'Connor: Can you share example prompts for 32k context? We want to see how we chunk medical notes.
[08:31] Arjun Patel: We'll include a prompt engineering doc and examples. For long notes we use prefixing, summaries of sections, and retrieval of relevant segments, or use models that natively support 32k.
[08:45] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Any red flags for our infra? We run Kubernetes with EKS, Postgres for storage, and a FHIR gateway.
[08:53] Arjun Patel: That's good. We'll integrate via secure connectors. For Private deployments on-prem we support air-gapped packages but that requires some work on your side for networking and KMS. For Dedicated we do VPC peering and secure peeks via private endpoints.
[09:06] Samir Gupta: Ok, on costs - can you show a sample per-summary cost at 10k summaries/day?
[09:12] Maya Chen: We'll run a cost model with your average prompt/response sizes. Generally Dedicated and caching reduce per-summary cost significantly compared to Hosted, especially at scale. We'll send a token estimator spreadsheet.
[09:25] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Regarding compliance, do you provide audit logs for every request and who accessed model outputs?
[09:31] Maya Chen: Yes - audit trails include request/response metadata, user IDs, and console actions. For PHI you can configure stricter retention and export logs to your SIEM.
[09:44] Liam O'Connor: About DR and backups for Private - any recommended patterns?
[09:49] Arjun Patel: We'll provide patterns; for Private you can use your own snapshotting and backup; we'll recommend cross-region replication for critical workloads.
[09:58] Dr. Elena Ruiz: If we want to fine-tune on our annotated set, what's the path?
[10:03] Arjun Patel: Fine-tuning on PHI requires Private or Dedicated flows; we'll need governance and a secure data pipeline. We can discuss options and whether instruction tuning is enough vs full fine-tune.
[10:18] Samir Gupta: One more: inference caching - how transparent is it? Can we evict caches on demand?
[10:24] Arjun Patel: Yes - cache controls are exposed; you can evict prefixes, control TTLs, and configure LRU policies per route.
[10:34] Maya Chen: We're at about 35 minutes in - want to do a quick recap and action items?
[10:39] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Yes please.
[10:41] Maya Chen: Recap: NexusMed needs 32k context summarization, multilingual clinical fidelity, PHI/data residency. Preferred path: start with Dedicated pilot in region, then migrate to Private for sensitive cohorts. We'll run benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic on your sample set, include tool-calling tests for EMR integration, and provide security docs.
[10:58] Liam O'Connor: That matches. Any blockers?
[11:00] Samir Gupta: Need internal security sign-off and budget approval. Also need the redacted dataset.
[11:07] Maya Chen: Action items spelled out - I'll send pricing and token estimator, Arjun will send benchmark plan, and we'll schedule POC kickoff for week of Oct 12.
[11:18] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Sounds good - thanks all.
[11:21] Maya Chen: Thanks - we'll follow up via email with docs and calendar invite. Bye!

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "function callin'" truncated), filler words, and overlaps. Intentional roughness retained to reflect raw Fireflies export.
